title: The Borg long-term memory inventory
description: Governance metadata for every durable memory artifact in The Borg. Declared intent only: the scanner in .bin/build-memory-inventory.py computes hashes, sizes, links, and review state into a separate gitignored snapshot and never writes back here. Validated by `.bin/build-memory-inventory.py validate`, which supports the keyword subset used below and rejects any schema keyword it does not implement.

version.description: Registry format version. Bump only for a breaking shape change.

defaults.description: Per-artifact-class defaults. A default supplies a field only when the individual record omits it; records always win. Keys are artifact types. Defaults are a concision device, never a substitute for per-artifact identity, rationale, or review history.

artifacts.description: One record per artifact, keyed by stable path-independent id. Generated mirrors and bridges get their own records; they are inventoried individually and reviewed for drift against `canonical_ref`.

artifactId.description: Stable, path-independent identifier. Lowercase kebab-case so ids survive relocation without churn.

artifactType.description: Artifact class from the taxonomy. Determines the semantic audit unit and the default review cadence.

visibility.description: public: record and path may live in the tracked registry. private: record must live only in a gitignored per-agent overlay. redacted: the artifact exists publicly but its record carries facts that may only be reported as aggregates.

canonicality.description: canonical: the authoritative text. generated: produced by tooling from `canonical_ref`. mirror: a hand-maintained or symlinked copy of `canonical_ref`. source: an ingested raw source that a knowledge_page cites.

loadMode.description: How the artifact enters a model's context, and therefore what it costs. `always` is fixed context cost; every other value is conditional.

risk.description: Consequence of this memory being stale or wrong, not its confidentiality. A `critical` artifact may override its class review cadence with a shorter one.

remediationPolicy.description: Permission tier for changes the audit proposes to this artifact. auto_safe is reachable only from interactive --apply and only for deterministic, reversible, content-preserving changes to generated artifacts or computed state. Deletion, archival, and destructive consolidation are approval_required regardless of what is written here.

pathRoot.description: Base the `path` resolves against. Generated Codex command bridges live under CODEX_HOME and agent Auto Memory lives under HOME, so paths are not all workspace-relative.

relativePath.description: Path relative to `path_root`. No leading slash and no `..` so a record can never point outside its declared root.

cadence.description: A named interval, or an event trigger written as `on_<event>` for artifacts reviewed on a condition rather than a clock.

reviewMethod.description: Atomic review methods. The design's illustrative compound token `semantic_and_best_practice` is written here as the array [semantic, best_practice] so the audit can select candidates by method without parsing compound names.

classDefaults.description: Flattened defaults for one artifact class, per the design's `defaults.scoped_rule` example. Only fields that are genuinely uniform across a class belong here; rationale, provenance, success signals, and retirement triggers are never defaultable because they are the per-artifact justification.

consumers.description: Harnesses, agents, jobs, or workflows that actually load this artifact. Drives orphan detection and the fixed-context estimate.

artifact.description: One durable memory artifact. Validated after class defaults are merged in, so a field satisfied by a default is not reported missing.

id.description: Optional restatement of the map key. When present it must match the key exactly; the validator enforces this.

canonical_ref.description: Id of the artifact this one is generated from or mirrors. Required for `generated` and `mirror`; forbidden otherwise.

rationale.description: Why the artifact exists and what failure it prevents. Not a description of its contents.

provenance.description: The decision, source, incident, requirement, or upstream feature that justified adding it.

last_reviewed.description: Date of the last completed substantive review. `null` means never reviewed, which is a legitimate state for a newly registered artifact and makes it a deep-review candidate. A failed or partial review must not advance this.

success_signals.description: Observable evidence that the artifact earns its place.

retirement_triggers.description: Concrete conditions that would justify relocation, consolidation, archival, or removal.

related.description: Ids of known dependencies, overlaps, replacements, or superseded items. May be empty. Every id must resolve; a public record may not reference a private one.
